Geographic focus:
    Middle East — Lebanon (southern Lebanon, Tyre; Israel operations)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — documents displacement and casualties since March 2
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — school year disruption starting September 15, ongoing displacement of 340,000+, shelter-to-school transitions uncertain
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — generational education loss, infrastructure destruction, no ceasefire in sight per Save the Children

Synopsis:
    Six months into renewed Israel-Hezbollah hostilities, over 340,000 Lebanese remain displaced, with thousands of children living in public schools repurposed as shelters. As the September 15 school year approaches, families face acute housing and education uncertainty. 50 public schools are destroyed, 200+ damaged, and the UN estimates at least 100,000 children's schooling is at risk. The humanitarian response is limited; NGOs and the education ministry are attempting partial reopenings, but a political resolution is identified as the only durable fix.
